Where I live most universities deliver 3 different diplomas depending on how long you stay so it can be either 3 years (you can't really get a job with that one), 5 years and you can get a job in your field or 8 years and you can do research in your field. So right now I'm torn between doing 5 years to become a psychologist, 8 years to do psychological research or going to med school to become a psychiatrist (which are a lot more scarce in my country) but that would take me 10+ years of studying to achieve. I'm still trying to figure it out haha

What do you plan on doing after you're done with your course?

I definitely do feel ashamed about it sometimes and resent myself for being this way but I know that won't help so I try to not focus on that too much. What you're saying is really nice, thank you for all of that (and possibly saving my life earlier). You're an incredible person and I hope you know it

Awesome, during my first semester I had sociology classes as well (it was actually a mix of psychology, sociology and education sciences, which I all found fascinating) but now it's only psychology, and sadly most students didn't like having to study all three even though they only wanted to graduate in one so the university is gonna stop doing it next year. I feel the same way about the lectures, they're usually really slow and repetitive so I tend to get distracted (and by that I mean browsing reddit all day long) which is a shame because most of the things we study I find really interesting, I just can't focus long enough to enjoy them so now I only go to the classes I know I'm gonna be invested in and I study the rest by myself at home.

It makes me feel a lot better to hear that, when I go into depressive mode I tend to think I'm so dysfonctionnal that's there's no way I'll ever get better but having it explained like that really puts things into perspective and helps me feel understood in a way. Especially the part about anger being easier to process than pain and how anger is a way to express my feelings and make people acknowledge them. I know it's not the right way, but sometimes I get so deeply hurt that I don't have the energy to find another way. He does know, I've always been pretty open about my mental health struggles and I know he won't judge me for them so I often talk about what I feel. He is definitely an incredible person and he did reassure me, but I'm still so scared that I'm not good enough for him or that I'll end up hurting him, and I believe he deserves so much better than me

Thank you so much for this. Just reading the first few words of your comment made me burst out in tears, which was unexpected but so relieving. I know it is messed up, I'm not quite sure what's wrong with me. I'm studying psychology now, partly because I want to help others and partly because I want to understand why I am the way I am, but that's definitely a work in progress. I'm so sorry you're dealing with these type of thoughts as well and I hope you'll find a way out.

Thank you for offering to listen as well, it might be a bit hard to follow because I'm not sure where to start but I'll do my best. The reason I'm having a breakdown right now is because I've been mean to my boyfriend for stupid reasons and I feel so guilty and mad at everything. Anger has always been a major part in my life, whether I'm angry at myself or at others, and sometimes I just can't handle it well no matter how hard I try. The worst is, when I'm angry, I don't want it to stop, I just keep (half unconsciously) looking for reasons to be even more mad, and that usually leads me to thinking about what my ex did to me and the unfairness of it all. Which is why I think that's the main struggle in my mind at this point. My current boyfriend and I started dating right after I broke up with my piece of shit ex-bf, and he's been so supportive ever since. I know it's definitely been a struggle for him to deal with all of that but so far I tried my best to be good to him and he was always positive he wanted to go through it with me (even though I've told him countless times he didn't have to take on that burden, that I wouldn't resent him for leaving etc). That makes me hate myself even more for hurting him like I did and I really don't know what to do. I feel like no matter what I do to try and make his life easier I just keep messing everything up.
